detail.longDescription: This question isn't specific to vibe-coded apps, I was just curious how many people are using bespoke everyday software, for things like a file explorer, terminal, maybe mail client, text editor etc. Down the line I had planned on writing my own terminal, text editor and file explorer, but had too many other high priority projects and hadn't gotten around to it yet, and probably wouldn't for another year. Playing with Claude, after only...six prompts, I have my ideal custom terminal...kitty graphics, iterm style tmux integration, transparency, renaming tabs, session support, other small stuff; it's tailored exactly to my workstyle and aesthetic tastes, and so far is working amazingly. I see why so much vibe-coded stuff gets released - because it's exciting to share having brought your vision to life. If I had written this pre-AI, I'd be proud of it and want to share, but now, if it only takes six prompts to generate, I'm not sure there would be a point?
